title: From Sensing to Shaping: Biomolecular Condensates Orchestrating Plant Signaling and Membranes
content: Plants cannot flee unfavorable conditions, so they must sense and respond to physical and biotic stress from within a single cell. Biomolecular condensates — protein- and RNA-rich assemblies formed by phase separation — have emerged as a unifying mechanism that lets plant cells convert continuous physical cues such as heat, drought and pathogen attack into discrete, reversible biochemical switches. This mini review synthesizes recent structural, biophysical and genetic evidence on how plant condensates assemble, how they sense the environment, how they are exploited and subverted during infection, and how they organize RNA processing and membrane remodeling.
